data.title: Baruch Hashem You Just Can’t Say It Enough

lyrics.text: Growing up I watched my mama
And my brothers’ clothes and mine were kind of tattered
But we had love and we had faith
And there was laughter in our home
So I guess we had the only things that mattered
Be it smooth be it rough
You just can’t say it enough
As the days and years flew by
If it wasn’t sad you’d say it’s kinda funny
That I’ve tried my very best
Just like my folks I’m not too good at making money
But Hashem knows what He’s doing
Why waste time in useless second guessing
Are but means to help us grow
So instead of counting money count your blessings
Be it smooth be it rough
You just can’t say it enough
There was a time not long ago
I’m not too proud to say
When I resented the good fortune of my friends
How I wish I could take back
As it brought me less than nothing in the end
But I’ve cast aside that burden
Growing up taught me a thing or two
Now I go around with my guitar
And sing for all to hear
The grass is mighty green on my side too
Be it smooth be it rough
You just can’t say it enough
Be it smooth be it rough
You just can’t say it enough
Let me tell you a story it may even be true
Bout a fella who fell through the cracks
He was a hustler a gambler who lived on the edge
And they called him Lucky Fingers Max
He’d wager and win at the track and the fights
Rolled sevens when he threw the dice
But if you asked him for a dime he’d laugh in your face
He was lucky but he wasn’t too nice
Had a heart as black as coal
Would he ever find would he ever find his lost Jewish soul
One day he got a tip from some friends of his in Jersey
Bout a fighter named Tiger Malone
His opponent’s gonna lay down in the seventh round
You oughta bet everything that you own
Lucky bet his money his house and his Caddy
Sat down to watch the fight with a snack
Things were going fine ‘til the end of the sixth
When Tiger dropped dead from a heart attack
His lucky life his lucky life had gone up in smoke
He was hiding from the cold in a worn-out Shul
When the Rabbi came over and said
Let me lend you some money from the Synagogue fund
You can buy yourself a coat and some bread
Rabbi Lucky said you don’t understand
I’m a gambler a hustler a cheat
All I see is a Jew the old Rabbi replied
Lucky took the money and went to the track
Put it all on Teapot Kelly to win
In a photo finish he won by a nose
Lucky Fingers was in business again
Three stories of precious stained glass
All it says on the plaque is the money came from heaven
Still has a long long way to go
And that is why what happened
On the day we were engaged
Had a diamond far more beautiful
Your parents said that I deserved
But little did I know how this
With the wedding just behind us
A week of music dance and song
I looked down at my hand and found
Your parents did not take it well
Found it quite hard to accept
Of each room in which we stepped
In a chill quite cold for spring
When from deep in your coat’s pocket
You pulled out my diamond ring
Look what I found you cried out
My dear you did no wrong
It was my fault all along
You were teased for quite a while
Were the source of many laughs
But years flew by and it became
Then I wished you were still here
And to comfort my unyielding ache
To clean out some old things
When in an old valise I found
As I viewed the stone and band
Of the ring worn on my hand
Now not a day goes by
And your sweet and boundless love
By the kindness you had shown
If what I’d lost not been found
If what I’d lost not been found
When they came on that cold winter day
And the boxcars that took us away
We held on to each other
But I only I would survive
That I’d buy for Mama each day
Then hand me a keichel and say
He made our world so very sweet
Siz gut tzu zayn a Yid
Mutek and I were two of a kind
Like brothers the very best of friends
Playing all day in the streets of the Shtetl
We would carry water to all of the shops
For only five groschen a pail
But first we’d learn Torah in our little shul
An hour or two without fail
I’ll never forget when the Shidduch was Redt
Papa came home with the news
In no time the match was approved
Blessed by the Heilige Rebbe himself
A date for the wedding was set
And whoever I met for the next week or two
Said to me soon you’ll be next
Laughter and joy could be felt in the air
With music heard all through the town
What a radiant bride my dear Roizah was
The groom looking handsome and strong
And after his shoe came down on the glass
The townsfolk all burst out into song
In the centre of the crowd
Mutek and I danced into the night
Round and round round and round
Round and round round and round
My grandmother whispered a secret to me
And placed something soft in my hands
My love for you is in every strand
But setting each stitch and knitting the rows
With patterns to form a design
And hours and hours of time
My grandfather whispered a secret to me
And showed me his old violin
As you would with a feather
Place the instrument under your chin
If you wish to bring forth its heavenly sound
Play music both haunting and sweet
And the crowd will rise up on its feet
My Rebbe whispered a secret to me
As he looked deep in my eyes
If you roll up your sleeves
I promise you after the sweat and the tears
You’ll be dancing with joy in the end
With summer approaching my kids said to me
There’s so little to do in the yard
You see Daddy it won’t be hard
Now go get my tools from the drawer
Then we’ll saw and we’ll bang
And tomorrow we’ll do it once more
Bezeias Apecha is the fate of all mankind
No one can avoid the bustle and the grind
Rushing to meetings closing the deal
On the phone on the road
It’s easy to lose balance chasing money and success
But there is a special treasure with which we have been blessed
And as each day passes joy fills the air
In the candle’s glow our neshomas grow
Once the wine is poured we become restored
We work hard and struggle just to make ends meet
But once out of seven we all become kings
As we learn and pray tension melts away
Home from shul we stride with Malachim at our side
I’m so stressed out at work
When I hear the boss I jump
To shop or go to shul
I’m always parking by a pump
When my wife and children join me
Mir shteigen hecher nenter tzum bashefer
We get to catch our breath
Making sure our lives have purpose
So let these words be on the lips
We were placed on earth for eternal worth
As much as all of the above
We get to bond with those we love
Our parents spend more time with us
Not much in life is absolute
Who will win the Super Bowl
But in the Igros Moshe’s view
One thing you can be sure is true

But he wrote that it’s guaranteed

Why this is so I know not
The food in that bowl sure seems hot
But that’s no cause to make a fuss
It’s all about in whom you trust
Rav Moshe said that it’s a fact
And that’s sure good enough for me

There ain’t no bishul in a kli shlishi

The size of its audience has expanded like a tidal wave
And it reaches all corners of the Jewish world and beyond

Represent virtually every genre of musical expression

Rechnitz songs to please the ear

But that’s just one part of this precious

We’ll soon forget it took so long
